DebugFindBorders.blurb: Intended to print verbose “find borders” debug lines while the nav-map quad-tree processor walks border cells. Default false. Flipping it does nothing in this tree: the logging macro is defined, but no call site ever expands it.
DebugFindBorders.detail: Registered next to RenderSeeds / RenderBorders* under category QuadTreeProcessor. A local DEBUG_FIND_BORDER macro gates channelled INFO on NMQTProcessor when this flag is true, but rg finds zero uses of that macro (or of kDebugFindBorders) outside the definition. Border-finding viz code that once consumed the sibling Render* flags is gone; only registration remains.
DebugFindBorders.statusNote: CONSOLE_VAR + unused debug macro only — never read at a call site.

DefaultMaxObservationDistance_mm.blurb: Maximum camera distance in millimeters at which a generic observable object (cube, custom object, etc.) is still accepted when the robot “sees” its markers. Default 500 mm; console range about 50–1000. Observations farther than this are dropped before they update block-world poses.
DefaultMaxObservationDistance_mm.detail: Returned by ObservableObject::GetMaxObservationDistance_mm() for types that do not override it. BlockWorld::FilterRawObservedObjects erases any raw observation whose last pose-update distance exceeds this value. The same number is used when estimating how much image border padding unobserved markers need (scale with distance / max distance). Chargers use a separate console var (ChargerMaxObservationDistance_mm) via Charger::GetMaxObservationDistance_mm override — this Default* knob does not move charger range.

EdgeLineLengthToInsert_mm.blurb: Half-length (mm) of the thin rectangular strip written into the navigation memory map when vision reports a table-edge / cliff line from overhead-edge detection. Default 200 mm. Larger values stamp a longer “wall” of cliff cells along the estimated edge; smaller values make shorter cliff marks.
EdgeLineLengthToInsert_mm.detail: MapComponent::AddVisionOverheadEdges, after refining cliff pose from Hough-style line fitting, inserts a FastPolygon whose lateral extents are ±EdgeLineLengthToInsert_mm and whose depth uses VisionCliffPadding_mm. Only runs when OverheadEdges vision results are processed into the map. Sibling Hough knobs (angle resolution, min line length, gap, accum threshold) control how the line is found; this var only sizes the map geometry that is inserted once a cliff pose is accepted.

MapRenderRate_sec.blurb: How often (seconds) the engine re-sends the full navigation memory map to the Viz 3D debug view when map rendering is enabled. Default 0.25 s (4 Hz). Lower values update Viz more often and use more clad/bandwidth; higher values throttle redraws.
MapRenderRate_sec.detail: MapComponent::UpdateDependent only paces BroadcastMapToViz with this rate. Viz send also requires ANKI_DEV_CHEATS draw enable, _isRenderEnabled (SetMemoryMapRenderEnabled game message / WebViz path), and a dirty map. WebViz navmap and SDK map broadcast use separate dirty flags / _broadcastRate_sec — this console var does not throttle those. Comment in code: clad was getting overloaded with too many quads at higher rates.
MapRenderRate_sec.howTo: 1) Enable memory-map render (SetMemoryMapRenderEnabled or WebViz navmap). 2) Set MapRenderRate_sec. 3) Drive so the map changes and watch Viz refresh rate.
MapRenderRate_sec.statusNote: Only affects Viz when map render is enabled and dev drawing is compiled in; does not change planning.

MaxObsThreshold_mm.blurb: Farthest distance (mm) the front time-of-flight “prox” sensor still counts as a real obstacle. Default 400 mm. Readings at or beyond this are treated as clear (unobstructed); closer valid readings can become map obstacles. Also clamps the published distance field up to this max.
MaxObsThreshold_mm.detail: ProxSensorComponent::NotifyOfRobotStateInternal: foundObject requires raw distance < MaxObsThreshold_mm (plus quality, lift not in FOV, valid range status, pitch in band). unobstructed is true when quality is low or raw distance ≥ Max. _latestData.distance_mm is Clamp(raw, MinObsThreshold, MaxObsThreshold). Raising the cap lets the robot map farther objects; lowering ignores distant hits and shrinks the usable clear-beam cone. Not used on Whiskey builds (early return).

MaxObstacleWidth_mm.blurb: Maximum lateral width (mm) of a prox-sensor obstacle stamp in the navigation map. Default 18 mm (about half a robot width). Even if the ToF beam would fan out wider at long range, the obstacle and clear-region math cap width at this value so far hits do not paint huge blocking blobs.
MaxObstacleWidth_mm.detail: ObstacleWidth(measurement) = min(measurement × SensorAperture, MaxObstacleWidth_mm). GetClearRegion uses the same cap: if the natural beam half-width is already under Max/2 it inserts a simple triangle; otherwise it intersects the wide cone with a clamped rectangle so clear space does not stretch awkwardly. Comment in code: uncapped far obstacles cause planning failures. Raising allows wider prox marks; lowering makes prox obstacles thinner/more precise but can leave uncleared flanks.

MergeOldMaps.blurb: When false (default), every previous navigation memory map is discarded whenever the robot creates a new localized map (new world origin). When true, maps whose pose origins are still “alive” (not zombie) are kept so they can be merged/reused across relocalization.
MergeOldMaps.detail: In CreateLocalizedMemoryMap, each stored map is deleted if BlockWorld::IsZombiePoseOrigin(origin) OR !MergeOldMaps. Default false therefore forces isZombie for every existing entry — wipe-all behavior. Enabling true only deletes origins that truly lost all localizable objects. Source comment still says “kNeverMergeOldMaps” but the registered id is MergeOldMaps. Affects how much historical cliff/prox/cube map survives delocalization; does not by itself re-run localization.
MergeOldMaps.howTo: Leave false for stock-like behavior (fresh map per origin). Set true only when debugging multi-origin map merge / zombie retention.

MinObsThreshold_mm.blurb: Closest distance (mm) reported for the front prox sensor after clamping. Default 30 mm. Sensor values nearer than this are pulled up to 30 so obstacle placement never uses near-zero depths that would sit inside the body.
MinObsThreshold_mm.detail: Applied only as Util::Clamp on _latestData.distance_mm together with MaxObsThreshold_mm. foundObject / unobstructed gates use the raw message distance against Max and quality/pitch/lift checks — they do not re-test Min. Raising Min makes very-near hits look farther when inserted; lowering allows deeper near-field values if the sensor reports them. Pair with Max when tuning the usable ToF window.

NumRandomObstacles.blurb: How many fixed custom-block obstacles the DockingTestSimple developer behavior scatters near the cube’s pre-dock pose before each docking trial. Default 10. Set 0 to skip obstacle injection. Only matters while that docking test behavior is running — not freeplay.
NumRandomObstacles.detail: When > 0, BehaviorDockingTestSimple deletes prior custom objects then CreateFixedCustomObject at random offsets around the pre-action pose (X in about −200…120 mm, Y ±300 mm, with a keep-out band so nothing sits directly in the approach lane). Obstacles are 10×10×50 mm. Used to stress path planning / docking under clutter. Behavior class is DockingTestSimple (dev/factory-style test), not production HighLevelAI.
NumRandomObstacles.howTo: 1) Run or select DockingTestSimple. 2) Set NumRandomObstacles (0 = clean). 3) Start a trial and watch custom obstacles appear near pre-dock.
NumRandomObstacles.statusNote: Live only inside BehaviorDockingTestSimple; ignored outside that dev behavior.

OverheadEdges.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::OverheadEdges so the vision system runs table-edge / ground-plane edge detection on camera frames. Results feed MapComponent, which can insert vision-derived cliffs into the navigation map (used e.g. when reacting to cliffs).
OverheadEdges.detail: Registered dynamically by VisionComponent::SetupVisionModeConsoleVars for every VisionMode enum name under category Vision.General.VisionModes. When toggled, EnableMode + DevOnly subscribe/unsubscribe schedule the mode. VisionSystem calls OverheadEdgesDetector::Detect; VisionComponent::UpdateOverheadEdges forwards OverheadEdgeFrame to MapComponent::ProcessVisionOverheadEdges. Behaviors such as ReactToCliff and a MapComponent console helper WaitForImagesAction(OverheadEdges) also request this mode. Edge geometry size uses EdgeLineLengthToInsert_mm after Hough refinement.
OverheadEdges.howTo: Toggle OverheadEdges on in console (or wait for a behavior that schedules it). Point the head at a table edge with ground plane visible. Watch map cliffs / debug images; tune EdgeLineLengthToInsert_mm and Hough* vars if marks are wrong.

OverheadMap.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::OverheadMap so the vision system warps the ground plane into a top-down RGB “overhead map” used for ground-pixel classification research (drivable vs non-drivable training data). Default product schedules normally leave this off; turning the console flag on runs UpdateOverheadMap when color images are available.
OverheadMap.detail: Same dynamic VisionMode console registration as OverheadEdges. VisionSystem constructs OverheadMap from vision_config.json “OverheadMap” (NumRows/NumCols). When the mode is enabled and the image has color, UpdateOverheadMap projects ground-plane pixels into the overhead canvas; comments note the path was kept while the mode was product-disabled. Related GroundPlaneClassifier / Obstacles mode consumes similar ground reasoning but is a separate VisionMode. Enabling this is mainly for vision debug and classifier data collection, not everyday navigation.
OverheadMap.howTo: 1) Enable OverheadMap in Vision.General.VisionModes. 2) Ensure color frames and a visible ground plane. 3) Inspect OverheadMap debug images / classifier training dumps if configured.

paths.notes: JSON key OverheadMap supplies NumRows/NumCols (and related) for the overhead canvas size.

OverheadMap.statusNote: Code path is live when the mode is forced on; stock scheduling may leave it unused in freeplay.

ProxExploredTriangleHalfWidth_mm.blurb: Half-width (mm) of the forward triangle used to mark prox-map obstacles as “explored” when the robot stands near them during explore-examine. Default 50 mm. Wider triangle covers more lateral prox cells per tick; narrower requires the robot to be more centered on the obstacle.
ProxExploredTriangleHalfWidth_mm.detail: MapComponent::FlagProxObstaclesUsingPose builds a triangle from the robot pose: apex at the robot, far points at length ProxExploredTriangleLength_mm and ± half-width. Any ObstacleProx cell inside is MarkExplored. Called from BehaviorExploringExamineObstacle before flood-fill of explored borders. Pure map metadata — does not change ToF hardware thresholds.

ProxExploredTriangleLength_mm.blurb: Forward length (mm) of the “explored” triangle painted from the robot when examine-obstacle marks nearby ToF obstacles as seen. Default 300 mm — shorter than full prox reach so the robot must get fairly close before cells flip to explored.
ProxExploredTriangleLength_mm.detail: Companion to ProxExploredTriangleHalfWidth_mm in FlagProxObstaclesUsingPose. Length is along the robot heading in the robot frame before transform to world. Exploring examine obstacle calls this every tick while active (non-activation check path). Longer values mark distant prox obstacles explored without approach; shorter forces closer inspection.

ProxTimeout_ms.blurb: How long (milliseconds of robot message time) a prox-sensor obstacle may sit on the navigation memory map without being re-observed before it is erased. Default 600,000 ms = 10 minutes.
ProxTimeout_ms.detail: MapComponent::TimeoutObjects runs about every TimeoutUpdatePeriod_ms. For EContentType::ObstacleProx, if last-observed time ≤ now − ProxTimeout_ms the node transform returns empty data (clears the cell). Other content types use their own timers (vision edges, cliffs, unrecognized). Raising keeps ghost ToF obstacles longer (planner keeps avoiding); lowering forgets them sooner so the robot may re-sense the space.

RenderBordersFrom.blurb: Was meant to draw the origin quad of each detected nav-map border for debugging. Default false. No remaining code reads this flag — border debug rendering was removed while the console var stayed.
RenderBordersFrom.detail: Registered in quadTreeProcessor.cpp with comment “renders detected borders (origin quad)”. Sibling vars RenderBordersToDot / ToQuad / Seeds / ZOffset / Border3DLines share the same fate. FillBorder / GetNodesToFill still implement fill logic but never consult these render switches.
RenderBordersFrom.statusNote: CONSOLE_VAR only; never referenced after registration.

RenderBordersToDot.blurb: Was meant to draw each detected border’s center as a debug dot. Default false. Unused in this tree — registration only.
RenderBordersToDot.detail: Same unused (dead) cluster as RenderBordersFrom / ToQuad / Seeds under QuadTreeProcessor. Changing it cannot affect Viz or WebViz navmap colors.
RenderBordersToDot.statusNote: CONSOLE_VAR only; never referenced after registration.

RenderBordersToQuad.blurb: Was meant to draw the destination quad of each detected nav-map border. Default false. Unused — no call sites read kRenderBordersToQuad.
RenderBordersToQuad.detail: Registered with RenderBordersFrom/ToDot/Seeds. Documented intent only; border-finding debug draw path is gone. Use live map broadcast (MapRenderRate_sec + render enabled) for actual map visualization instead.
RenderBordersToQuad.statusNote: CONSOLE_VAR only; never referenced after registration.

RenderGazeDirectionPoints.blurb: When true, draws debug cuboids in Viz for where a tracked face is currently looking (orange = current gaze ground point, green = stable average gaze). Default false. Only runs if the GazeDirection product feature gate is also enabled.
RenderGazeDirectionPoints.detail: FaceWorld drawing path: after DrawHumanHead for the face, if this flag and FeatureType::GazeDirection are on, looks up _gazeDirection[faceId] and DrawCuboid at current and (if stable) average gaze directions with fixed viz object ids starting at 2345. Visualization only — does not change gaze estimation, behaviors, or nav map. Feature gate off ⇒ flag is a no-op even when true.
RenderGazeDirectionPoints.howTo: 1) Ensure feature GazeDirection is enabled. 2) Enable RenderGazeDirectionPoints. 3) Look at a tracked face in Viz and confirm orange/green ground cuboids.

RenderProxBeliefs.blurb: When true, navigation-map quads for ToF prox obstacles are colored as a cyan→green gradient by obstacle confidence (0–100) instead of a flat cyan style. Default false. Affects Viz/WebViz/SDK map broadcast colors only — not whether obstacles exist or how planning treats them.
RenderProxBeliefs.detail: memoryMap.cpp GetNodeVizColor: for EContentType::ObstacleProx, scale = clamp(GetObstacleConfidence()/100). ObstacleProx color = CYAN*scale + GREEN*(1−scale). Consumed when building MapBroadcastData quad colors for every leaf node. Pair with MapRenderRate_sec and render-enabled to see updates in Viz. Category string is ProxSensorComponent though the read is in MemoryMap broadcast.

RenderSeeds.blurb: Was meant to highlight “seed” quads differently when debugging nav-map border fill. Default false. Never read after registration — dead viz toggle.
RenderSeeds.detail: Registered at top of quadTreeProcessor.cpp with the RenderBorders* cluster. GetNodesToFill / FillBorder implement seed expansion for fill but do not branch on kRenderSeeds. Same dead status as RenderZOffset / RenderBorder3DLines documented in navmap-quadtree.json.
RenderSeeds.statusNote: CONSOLE_VAR only; never referenced after registration.
